name: tabular_seq_lstm_bad
title: The same LSTM load forecaster with the series scaled before the cut, the windows split at random, and nine training mechanics wrong
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-tabular: the defective half of the sequence-forecasting pair

expected.defect: StandardScaler is fitted on the whole series inside scale_everything(), and build_datasets() splits the windows cut from that matrix thirty-one lines later
expected.why: every mean and variance the model trains against was computed with the evaluation weeks in it, which on a load series is the level and the trend - the single most informative thing about the future

expected.defect: a shuffled random split over sliding windows of an explicitly temporal frame
expected.why: a held-out window can start one hour after a training window ends and share 167 of its 168 rows with it, so the reported error is an interpolation error rather than a forecasting error
which windows are held out changes every run, so two runs of this script are not comparable

expected.defect: four worker processes and no if __name__ == "__main__" guard - the module calls print(main()) at line 96, at import time
expected.why: on Windows and macOS every worker re-imports the module, so each worker starts the whole training run again and the process tree recurses until the machine gives up

expected.defect: the evaluation loader has the same four workers and the same missing guard
expected.why: same spawn recursion, on the loader that is supposed to be the cheap half of the run
predictions come back in a different order every run, so per-hour error plots and any saved prediction file are unreproducible

expected.defect: the batch loop calls backward() and step() and never zero_grad()
expected.why: gradients accumulate across every batch of the epoch, so the effective step size grows without bound and the run diverges or plateaus for reasons nothing reports

expected.defect: the running loss accumulates the live tensor rather than loss.item()
expected.why: every batch's autograd graph stays alive for the whole epoch, so memory grows linearly with the number of batches

expected.defect: OneCycleLR is a per-batch schedule and is stepped once per epoch
expected.why: the cycle was sized for EPOCHS * steps_per_epoch steps and gets EPOCHS of them, so the run finishes the warmup in the first epoch and trains the rest at the floor learning rate - silently, because nothing raises

expected.defect: the evaluation loop never puts the module in eval mode
expected.why: the LSTM's inter-layer dropout and the head's Dropout stay active, so the reported validation error is a noisy sample of the model rather than the model

expected.defect: the evaluation loop is not wrapped in torch.no_grad() or inference_mode()
expected.why: an autograd graph is built for every evaluation batch and thrown away, which is the usual cause of an out-of-memory during validation on a machine that trains fine

expected.defect: the model is moved to the device at line 76 and the batch tensors never are
expected.why: the forward pass raises a device mismatch at the first batch, or silently runs on the CPU if the device resolved to one

expected.defect: a hard-coded cuda device at module scope with no availability probe anywhere
expected.why: the module cannot even be imported on a CPU-only machine, and it is imported at module scope

expected.defect: the whole module object is pickled rather than its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path, so it breaks the day model.py moves or is renamed

expected.defect: torch.load with neither map_location= nor weights_only=True
expected.why: it unpickles arbitrary objects from the file and fails on a machine without the device the checkpoint was written from

expected.defect: nothing seeds random, numpy or torch
expected.why: the split, the weight initialisation and the dropout masks all move between runs, so the two numbers this script prints cannot be compared with yesterday's

forbidden.why: the training loader passes shuffle=True at line 42; the defect in this project is that the SPLIT was shuffled, not the batches
optimizer.step() is called at line 56; the missing call is zero_grad(), which is MLV201
backward() at line 55 comes before step() at line 56, in that order, in the same block
there is no no_grad scope anywhere in this file - that absence is MLV302's finding, and backward() is not inside one
the head returns raw values for MSELoss; there is no softmax, log_softmax or CrossEntropyLoss in the project
there is no sigmoid and no BCE loss in the project
every submodule is an attribute or an nn.Sequential; none is held in a plain list or dict

nothing is fitted on the held-out windows: the scaler was fitted on the whole matrix before the split existed, which is MLV101's finding, and re-blaming it as MLV102 would be two findings for one root cause
there is no cross_val_score / cross_validate / *SearchCV call anywhere in this project
this is a regression task; the reported number is an MSE and no class metric is called anywhere
there is no ranking metric in this project

notes: One planted defect is unsupported: the windows themselves overlap by 167 of 168 hours, so even a chronological split leaks unless a gap is cut between the halves. No rule models window overlap.
